items.label: f03-authn-vs-authz
items.front: How do Umami read routes split authentication from authorization?
items.back: parseRequest authenticates (checkAuth: bearer or share token) and returns 401 when neither works; the handler then authorizes explicitly with a can* function such as canViewWebsite (admin, share-token ids, owner, team member). Forgetting the can* call is the classic IDOR.

items.label: f01-send-pipeline
items.front: List the main steps of POST /api/send in order.
items.back: Zod parse with skipAuth; read the x-umami-cache token; fetchWebsite on a cache miss (400 if missing); client info (IP, UA, geo); bot check (200 beep boop) then IP block (403); sessionId = v5 hash; createSession on the relational path when not cached; visitId with 30-minute expiry; saveEvent; return a fresh signed cache token.

items.label: f02-two-token-strategies
items.front: What are Umami's two login token strategies, and what is the tradeoff?
items.back: With Redis: saveAuth stores { userId, role } under auth:<random> and returns an encrypted token wrapping that key, so the session can be revoked by deleting the key. Without Redis: createSecureToken returns a self-contained encrypted token with userId and role, which cannot be revoked server-side.

items.prompt: How does the pixel route p/[slug] record a hit before it returns its 1x1 GIF?

choices.text: It builds a synthetic event Request and awaits the send POST
It inserts a websiteEvent row itself with Prisma directly
It publishes the hit to Kafka and returns without waiting
It redirects the browser to /api/send with query params

choices: It builds a synthetic event Request and awaits the send POST
It inserts a websiteEvent row itself with Prisma directly
It publishes the hit to Kafka and returns without waiting
It redirects the browser to /api/send with query params

items.explanation: The route builds { type: "event", payload: { pixel: id, url, referrer } } into a new POST Request (reusing the inbound headers) and calls await POST(req) from the send route, so pixels share the whole collection pipeline. Then it returns the GIF.

items.prompt: The recorder posts 50 events to /api/record without an x-umami-cache header. What does the route answer?

choices.text: 200 ok, and a new session is created for it
200 ok false, with reason replay_disabled
400 with the message Missing session token.
401 Unauthorized, from the skipAuth guard

choices: 200 ok, and a new session is created for it
200 ok false, with reason replay_disabled
400 with the message Missing session token.
401 Unauthorized, from the skipAuth guard

items.explanation: Replay cannot start a session: without the x-umami-cache header the route returns badRequest({ message: "Missing session token." }). A header that parses but lacks sessionId or visitId gets "Invalid session token." instead.

items.prompt: A valid replay chunk with a valid session token arrives for a website whose replayEnabled is false. What does /api/record return?

choices.text: 403 Forbidden with Business subscription required
200 { ok: true }, and the chunk is stored anyway
400 Bad request with Website not found.
200 { ok: false, reason: "replay_disabled" }

choices: 403 Forbidden with Business subscription required
200 { ok: true }, and the chunk is stored anyway
400 Bad request with Website not found.
200 { ok: false, reason: "replay_disabled" }

items.explanation: The route reads the website directly with getWebsite (bypassing the Redis cache so the flag is fresh) and returns json({ ok: false, reason: "replay_disabled" }) when replay is off. The business-subscription 403 is a later CLOUD_MODE check.

items.prompt: Login is tried once with an unknown username and once with a known username and a wrong password. How do the two responses differ?

choices.text: Unknown user gets 401, wrong password gets 403
Unknown user gets 404, wrong password gets 401
They are identical, both 401 incorrect-username-password
Both get 400, with a field error for the input

choices: Unknown user gets 401, wrong password gets 403
Unknown user gets 404, wrong password gets 401
They are identical, both 401 incorrect-username-password
Both get 400, with a field error for the input

items.explanation: The route evaluates !user || !checkPassword(...) in one condition and returns the same unauthorized({ code: "incorrect-username-password" }) for either case, so the response does not reveal whether the username exists.

items.prompt: A tracker payload includes id: "user-42". How is sessionId computed for that request?

choices.text: A random v4 uuid, stored against user-42 for later lookups
uuid(sourceId, ip, userAgent, salt), the same as without id
uuid(id, ip): the website id is dropped from the hash input
uuid(sourceId, id): the IP and user agent are not used

choices: A random v4 uuid, stored against user-42 for later lookups
uuid(sourceId, ip, userAgent, salt), the same as without id
uuid(id, ip): the website id is dropped from the hash input
uuid(sourceId, id): the IP and user agent are not used

items.explanation: When the payload carries an id, the handler uses uuid(sourceId, id); otherwise it hashes source, IP, user agent and the rotating salt. uuid with arguments is a deterministic v5 UUID of their hash plus secret(), so the same id on another device maps to the same session.

items.prompt: A script sends a valid share token in x-umami-share-token, with no bearer token and no x-umami-share-context header. What does checkAuth return?

choices.text: null, as a share token needs the context header
An Auth object with shareToken set and the user left null
It throws, and the route answers with a 500
An Auth for the user who created the share

choices: null, as a share token needs the context header
An Auth object with shareToken set and the user left null
It throws, and the route answers with a 500
An Auth for the user who created the share

items.explanation: checkAuth returns null when there is no user and no share token, and also when there is a share token but no user and the share-context header is missing. parseRequest turns null into 401, so a share token only works from share pages that send both headers.

items.prompt: POST /api/send carries a website id that does not exist, and there is no x-umami-cache header. What does the handler return?

choices.text: 404 Not Found, from fetchWebsite returning null
400 Bad request with the message Website not found.
401 Unauthorized, since the website has no owner at all
200 with beep boop, as unknown ids are ignored

choices: 404 Not Found, from fetchWebsite returning null
400 Bad request with the message Website not found.
401 Unauthorized, since the website has no owner at all
200 with beep boop, as unknown ids are ignored

items.explanation: When there is no cached websiteId, the handler calls fetchWebsite and, on null, returns badRequest({ message: "Website not found." }), a 400. The guide table says 404, but the code answers 400; the code is keyed.

items.prompt: A request to /api/send comes from a blocked IP and also has a bot user agent (DISABLE_BOT_CHECK unset). What does the handler respond?

choices.text: A 200 JSON body { beep: "boop" }, nothing saved
400 Bad request, because bots fail the Zod schema
200 with a cache token, and the event is stored
403 Forbidden, since the IP block is checked first

choices: A 200 JSON body { beep: "boop" }, nothing saved
400 Bad request, because bots fail the Zod schema
200 with a cache token, and the event is stored
403 Forbidden, since the IP block is checked first

items.explanation: The bot check (isbot on the user agent) runs before hasBlockedIp, and it returns json({ beep: "boop" }) with status 200. The IP block never gets a chance to answer 403, and no event or session is written.

items.prompt: SALT_ROTATION is not set. Over what window does the same visitor (same IP and user agent, no id) keep the same sessionId?

choices.text: A single day, since the salt is built from startOfDay
One hour, which is the window of the visit salt too
A calendar month, as getSalt defaults to startOfMonth
Forever, as no salt is mixed in without the variable

choices: A single day, since the salt is built from startOfDay
One hour, which is the window of the visit salt too
A calendar month, as getSalt defaults to startOfMonth
Forever, as no salt is mixed in without the variable

items.explanation: The handler uses process.env.SALT_ROTATION || "month", and getSalt hashes startOfMonth(createdAt) unless the value is day or week. The guide row says "same visitor+day+salt", but by default the session salt changes monthly; the hourly salt is for visits, not sessions.

items.prompt: The recorder posts to /api/record with a valid website id, events: [], and no x-umami-cache header. What comes back?

choices.text: 400 Missing session token, from the header check below
200 { ok: true }, as the empty batch returns early
400 Bad request, since Zod requires at least one event
403 Forbidden, because replay needs a session

choices: 400 Missing session token, from the header check below
200 { ok: true }, as the empty batch returns early
400 Bad request, since Zod requires at least one event
403 Forbidden, because replay needs a session

items.explanation: The events array may be empty (only max(200) is enforced). Right after parsing, if (!events?.length) return json({ ok: true }) runs before the session-token check, so the missing header never matters.

items.prompt: A GET to an authenticated read route has no Authorization header and a query that fails the route's Zod schema. What status does parseRequest produce?

choices.text: 200, as the error is only logged by parseRequest
401, because authentication always runs before validation
403, since the request has neither user nor share
400, as checkAuth is skipped once validation fails

choices: 200, as the error is only logged by parseRequest
401, because authentication always runs before validation
403, since the request has neither user nor share
400, as checkAuth is skipped once validation fails

items.explanation: parseRequest validates first; on failure it sets error to badRequest(...). Authentication runs only when !options?.skipAuth && !error, so with an error already set checkAuth is never called and the caller sees 400.

items.prompt: Redis is enabled. After a successful login, how long does the auth:<key> entry that saveAuth wrote stay in Redis?

choices.text: It has no TTL; login calls saveAuth without expire
30 minutes, the same window as a tracked visit
7 days, matching the token's encrypted expiry
24 hours, which is the default expire value of saveAuth

choices: It has no TTL; login calls saveAuth without expire
30 minutes, the same window as a tracked visit
7 days, matching the token's encrypted expiry
24 hours, which is the default expire value of saveAuth

items.explanation: saveAuth(data, expire = 0) sets an expiry only when expire is truthy, and the login route calls saveAuth({ userId, role }) with no second argument. The key therefore stays until something deletes it; revocation is possible because it lives server-side.

items.prompt: A non-admin user with no share token asks for metrics of a website owned by a team they do not belong to. What does canViewWebsite return?

choices.text: false, but only after it throws a 403 error itself
true, because team websites are readable by all
true, since any signed-in user may view metrics
false, as getTeamUser finds no team membership

choices: false, but only after it throws a 403 error itself
true, because team websites are readable by all
true, since any signed-in user may view metrics
false, as getTeamUser finds no team membership

items.explanation: There is no admin bypass and no share-token match. The entity has a teamId, not a userId, so the function returns !!(await getTeamUser(teamId, user.id)), which is false for a non-member. canViewWebsite returns a boolean; the route decides the status.
